articles.title: IPCA: inflação de outubro fica em 0,14% e supera teto da meta  | G1
articles.standfirst: Índice acumulou alta de 4,63% em 12 meses, acima do limite de 4,5% da meta de inflação. Alta dos alimentos, puxada pelo tomate, pressionou os preços no mês, segundo o IBGE.
articles.summary: IPCA de outubro sobe 0,14% com pressão dos alimentos, enquanto a queda nas passagens aéreas e na conta de luz evitou uma alta maior da inflação oficial.
articles.body:
O Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA), considerado a inflação oficial do país, subiu 0,14% em outubro. O resultado foi divulgado nesta quinta-feira (12) pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

O indicador desacelerou em relação a setembro, quando o índice avançou 0,82% , a maior alta para o mês desde 2021.

Apesar da desaceleração, a inflação acumulada em 12 meses chegou a 4,63% , acima do teto de 4,5% da meta estabelecida pelo Conselho Monetário Nacional (CMN). No acumulado do ano, os preços subiram 4,10%. Em outubro de 2025, a inflação havia sido de 0,09%.

🔍 A meta central de inflação é de 3% , com margem de tolerância de 1,5 ponto percentual para cima ou para baixo. Pelo sistema de metas contínuas, a meta só é considerada descumprida quando a inflação permanece fora desse intervalo por seis meses consecutivos.

Segundo o IBGE, Alimentação e bebidas foi o grupo que registrou a maior alta de preços em outubro, de 1,04%, e o que mais pressionou a inflação no mês.

Em contrapartida, os preços caíram nos grupos de Transportes (-0,59%) e Habitação (-0,51%). Os demais grupos tiveram aumentos que variaram de 0,07% em Educação a 0,71% em Comunicação .

IPCA subiu 0,14% em outubro, impulsionado pelo preços dos alimentos — Foto: Arte g1

Veja a variação dos grupos pesquisados pelo IPCA

Inflação acumulada em 12 meses chegou a 4,63%, acima do teto de 4,5% da meta estabelecida pelo Conselho Monetário Nacional (CMN) — Foto: Arte g1

Alimentos voltam a pesar no bolso, com destaque para o tomate

Os preços dos alimentos voltaram a subir com mais força em outubro. O grupo Alimentação e bebidas registrou alta de 1,04%, acima dos 0,83% de setembro. Entre os produtos consumidos em casa, a alta foi ainda maior, passando de 0,96% em setembro para 1,31% em outubro.

O principal destaque foi o tomate, que ficou 19,57% mais caro em outubro . O produto já havia registrado alta de 37,76% em setembro e acumula aumento de 89,76% no ano. Nos últimos 12 meses, a elevação chega a 63,35%.

Outros alimentos também ficaram mais caros em outubro:

Em 12 meses, a cebola acumula alta de 108,21% , enquanto as carnes ficaram 12,09% mais caras.

Nem todos os produtos, porém, ficaram mais caros. A cenoura apresentou queda de 9,72%, seguida pela batata-inglesa (-2,95%) e pelo café moído (-1,03%).

Já os preços da alimentação fora de casa subiram em ritmo menor, passando de 0,48% em setembro para 0,36% em outubro. As refeições ficaram 0,39% mais caras, enquanto os lanches tiveram alta de 0,32%.

Passagens aéreas e conta de luz ficam mais baratas

O grupo Transportes registrou queda de 0,59% em outubro, puxada principalmente pela redução nos preços das passagens aéreas , que ficaram 9,21% mais baratas após uma alta de 9,66% em setembro.

Os combustíveis também recuaram, em média, 0,31%, após subirem 1,41% no mês anterior.

A gasolina ficou 0,56% mais barata, enquanto o gás veicular caiu 0,46%. Já o diesel e o etanol registraram altas de 1,66% e 1,02%, respectivamente.

🔍 A variação dos preços dos combustíveis ocorre em meio às medidas adotadas pelo governo para conter os efeitos da alta dos preços internacionais do petróleo, pressionados pela guerra no Oriente Médio.

Em outubro, a subvenção ao diesel foi prorrogada por mais 30 dias. Já em novembro, o governo estendeu a desoneração da gasolina e do etanol pelo mesmo período. O objetivo das medidas é reduzir a pressão dos combustíveis sobre a inflação.

No grupo Habitação , os preços caíram 0,51%, principalmente devido à queda de 1,92% na energia elétrica residencial . Em setembro, a conta de luz havia ficado 7,98% mais cara.

A queda ocorreu com a entrada em vigor da bandeira tarifária verde , que não prevê cobrança adicional na conta de energia. O resultado também refletiu mudanças nas tarifas de algumas cidades.

Ainda em Habitação , a tarifa de água e esgoto caiu 1,77%, influenciada por um desconto de 25% na tarifa mínima em Curitiba. Na cidade, o serviço ficou 16,14% mais barato.

Já o grupo Comunicação registrou alta de 0,71%, pressionado pelos aumentos nos preços do acesso à internet (3,82%) e dos planos de telefonia móvel (0,74%).

Entre as regiões pesquisadas pelo IBGE, Belém registrou a maior inflação de outubro, de 0,70%, impulsionada principalmente pelos aumentos nos preços do tomate (17,30%) e da energia elétrica residencial (1,59%).

Na outra ponta, Curitiba registrou a maior queda de preços, de 0,67%, influenciada pela redução nos preços das passagens aéreas (-11,58%) e da tarifa de água e esgoto (-16,14%).

articles.title: 'É o pior momento em quase 5 anos': por que as ações do Banco do Brasil derretem quase 10% na Bolsa | G1
articles.standfirst: Resultado do terceiro trimestre de 2026 ficou abaixo das expectativas do mercado, pressionado pelo aumento da inadimplência no agronegócio. Banco também reduziu sua previsão de lucro para 2026.
articles.summary: Resultado do terceiro trimestre de 2026 ficou abaixo das expectativas do mercado, pressionado pelo aumento da inadimplência no agronegócio.
articles.body:
As ações do Banco do Brasil ( BBAS3 ) lideravam as perdas do Ibovespa nesta quinta-feira (12), após a divulgação de um balanço do terceiro trimestre considerado muito abaixo das expectativas do mercado.

Por volta das 11h45 (horário de Brasília), os papéis derretiam 9,30%, cotados a R$ 15,32. As ações da BB Seguridade (BBSE3) , empresa de seguros e previdência controlada pelo banco, também recuavam 3,53%, a R$ 38,26.

"A ação chegou a atingir o pior patamar desde o final de 2021 e o início de 2022. É o pior nível em quase cinco anos. Realmente, é um momento bastante difícil", crava Daniel Utsch, gestor da Nero Capital

Em relatório divulgado nesta quinta, o BTG Pactual classificou o resultado do Banco do Brasil como "muito fraco" e destacou uma combinação de:

e redução das perspectivas de lucro e distribuição de dividendos .

"Na verdade, o resultado foi ainda pior quando se olha o lucro antes dos impostos. O Banco do Brasil teve um resultado negativo de R$ 1 bilhão nessa linha, mesmo com pouco mais de R$ 3 bilhões positivos na linha de impostos. Foi o pior resultado da série histórica nesse indicador", afirma o gestor da Nero.

Para os analistas do banco, os problemas enfrentados pela instituição vão além de uma dificuldade passageira e também envolvem questões estruturais do setor bancário.

O lucro líquido ajustado do Banco do Brasil foi de R$ 1,27 bilhão no terceiro trimestre, uma queda de 68% em relação ao trimestre anterior e de 66% na comparação com o mesmo período de 2025. O resultado ficou cerca de 60% abaixo do esperado pelo mercado, segundo o BTG.

Um dos principais fatores por trás do desempenho foi o aumento das provisões para perdas com empréstimos . Essas provisões são reservas que os bancos precisam separar para cobrir o risco de não receber o dinheiro emprestado.

No trimestre, o custo do crédito chegou a R$ 21,2 bilhões, alta de 15% em relação ao segundo trimestre e de 18% na comparação anual.

A situação é especialmente delicada no agronegócio , uma das principais frentes de atuação do Banco do Brasil.

A formação de novos casos de inadimplência no segmento saltou de R$ 5,7 bilhões no segundo trimestre para R$ 14,7 bilhões no terceiro. Com isso, o índice de atrasos superiores a 90 dias no agro subiu para 6,92%, avanço de 0,65 ponto percentual em três meses.

Daniel Utsch, da Nero Capital, explica que existe uma conjuntura de mudanças na legislação e nas políticas públicas que favorece um comportamento negativo.

"A MP 1.376 criou linhas de crédito para ajudar produtores rurais a pagar ou renegociar dívidas. Isso cria o que o mercado chama de moral hazard, ou risco moral: o produtor pode ficar mais propenso a deixar de pagar e buscar uma renegociação ou até uma recuperação judicial, caso enxergue um resultado mais favorável para si nessa alternativa do que tentando pagar o que deve", explica.

O BTG também chamou a atenção para a piora na pontualidade dos pagamentos.

Segundo informações apresentadas pela administração do banco, o percentual de clientes que pagavam suas parcelas em dia caiu de aproximadamente 80% até agosto para 76% em setembro e 66% em outubro.

Durante a apresentação dos resultados, o diretor financeiro do Banco do Brasil, Geovanne Tobias, atribuiu parte da deterioração a casos de produtores médios e grandes que, segundo ele, não estariam dispostos a pagar suas dívidas mesmo diante das condições favoráveis de renegociação oferecidas pelo banco.

O executivo classificou esse comportamento como risco moral e afirmou que esses clientes não voltarão a fazer negócios com a instituição.

Na avaliação do BTG, a consequência será uma redução significativa da exposição do banco ao agronegócio . Os analistas ressaltam, porém, que esse processo não será simples nem rápido, especialmente diante do volume de dívidas que ainda pode se transformar em inadimplência nos próximos trimestres.

As dificuldades também aparecem em outras linhas de crédito.

Entre pessoas físicas, o índice de inadimplência subiu para 9,14%, ante 8,41% no trimestre anterior. No cartão de crédito, chegou a 16,35%. Já entre pequenas e médias empresas, o indicador permaneceu elevado, em 9,46%.

Diante desse cenário, o Banco do Brasil revisou para baixo suas projeções para 2026.

A instituição passou a estimar um lucro líquido ajustado entre R$ 9 bilhões e R$ 11 bilhões , ante expectativas anteriores do mercado próximas de R$ 16 bilhões. O ponto médio da nova projeção, de R$ 10 bilhões, representa uma redução de aproximadamente 38% em relação ao consenso anterior.

Na prática, a revisão indica que o banco não espera uma recuperação expressiva no último trimestre do ano. Pela estimativa média, o lucro entre outubro e dezembro seria de R$ 1,4 bilhão, apenas 10% acima do registrado no terceiro trimestre.

O BTG também destacou a pressão sobre o capital da instituição, ou seja, os recursos que funcionam como uma proteção financeira para absorver perdas e sustentar as operações.

O indicador de capital principal do banco caiu 0,47 ponto percentual no trimestre, para 10,8%, abaixo dos cerca de 11% considerados preferíveis pela própria administração.

Para preservar esses recursos, o Banco do Brasil reduziu de 30% para 25% a parcela do lucro que pretende distribuir aos acionistas em 2026.

Também suspendeu as distribuições antecipadas de dividendos que ainda estavam previstas para este ano e informou que não fará pagamentos intermediários em 2027.

A possibilidade de reter até parte dos dividendos mínimos obrigatórios também foi mencionada pela administração, caso as condições de capital exijam.

Na avaliação do BTG, a combinação desses fatores ajuda a explicar por que as ações ainda podem sofrer novas perdas, mesmo sendo negociadas a um preço que, à primeira vista, parece baixo em relação ao patrimônio do banco.

"Não nos surpreenderíamos se a ação corrigisse ainda mais", afirmaram os analistas. Eles avaliam que os problemas do Banco do Brasil não se resumem a um ciclo temporário de aumento da inadimplência, mas também refletem mudanças estruturais no sistema bancário brasileiro.

O banco manteve recomendação neutra para BBAS3, com preço-alvo de R$ 18. O BTG também afirmou que vê risco relevante de novas revisões para baixo nas expectativas de lucro do Banco do Brasil em 2027, atualmente próximas de R$ 23 bilhões.

articles.title: BB: agronegócio esperou perdão de dívidas e aumentou inadimplência | G1
articles.standfirst: Banco registrou lucro líquido ajustado de R$ 1,27 bilhão no terceiro trimestre, uma queda de 66,5% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, informou a instituição na quarta (11).
articles.summary: A inadimplência do agronegócio e a expectativa pela MP 1376 de dívidas rurais explicam a queda de 66,5% no lucro do Banco do Brasil no terceiro trimestre.
articles.body:
O tombo no resultado do Banco do Brasil (BB) tem boa parte da sua explicação na promessa eleitoral para setores do agro de que a medida provisória (MP) da renegociação de dívidas rurais fosse trazer um perdão amplo e generoso.

Foi o aumento da inadimplência de produtores rurais, em especial de médio e grande porte, que derrubou o resultado do banco no período.

Até dezembro de 2025, o índice de produtores rurais pagando em dia observado pelo BB era de 95%. A partir de abril de 2026, o percentual caiu para 85%. Na semana anterior ao 1º turno das eleições, nova redução, para cerca de 79%. E entre o 1º e o 2º turno, o índice caiu ainda mais, para 69% e, na sequência, 56%.

O detalhamento de onde está a inadimplência não deixa dúvidas da conexão politica-eleitoral com o tombo nos pagamentos.

🚜 A inadimplência se concentra em médios e grandes produtores de soja, milho e pecuária, localizados na maioria em estados do Centro-Oeste. Sem quebras de safra ou impactos climáticos relevantes.

A evolução da inadimplência também chama a atenção. Ela é recente, já que 85% desses clientes deixaram de pagar a partir de 2024.

Entre setembro e outubro deste ano, na medida em que se aproximava o período eleitoral, os pagamentos em dia caíram ainda mais.

A situação se assemelha com movimentos de empresas quando há expectativa de que um governo anuncie uma renegociação de dívidas, os conhecidos regimes de recuperação fiscal. Na espera da renegociação, muitas empresas param de pagar.

No agro, parte dos produtores aguardava que a MP 1376, votada ontem no Senado Federal, trouxesse uma solução ainda mais benéfica – talvez milagrosa. Era o que apregoavam alguns políticos com trânsito no agro.

O foco da MP é o agricultor que teve perdas relevantes por conta de eventos climáticos. A promessa de alguns políticos em campanha era estender uma ajuda generalizada, que não veio.

💰 O texto ainda passará por possíveis ajustes e vetos, mas produtores rurais que caíram no conto eleitoral terão que reavaliar suas estratégias.

articles.title: Petrobras anuncia compra de empresa de transporte de etanol por R$ 620 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Com a operação, estatal passará a controlar 100% da empresa, que opera uma rede de dutos de mais de mil quilômetros para transporte de etanol. Negócio ainda depende de aprovação do Cade.
articles.summary: Com a operação, estatal passará a controlar 100% da empresa, que opera uma rede de dutos de mais de mil quilômetros para transporte de etanol.
articles.body:
Logo da Petrobras no Rio de Janeiro — Foto: Ricardo Moraes/Reuters

A Petrobras fechou um acordo para adquirir os 70% restantes da Logum Logística em uma transação de R$ 620 milhões , anunciou a estatal nesta quinta-feira (12).

Com a compra da fatia atualmente detida por Raízen Energia (30%), Copersucar (30%) e Uniduto Logística S.A. (10%), a Petrobras passará a controlar 100% da empresa de transporte , movimentação e armazenagem de etanol, outros biocombustíveis e derivados de petróleo.

Em comunicado, a Petrobras afirmou que o negócio a posiciona no "principal corredor logístico de etanol do país" e destacou o crescimento do mercado do biocombustível, especialmente com a expansão da produção de etanol de milho no Centro-Oeste.

🔎 A Logum opera uma rede de dutos com mais de mil quilômetros de extensão e terminais em Uberaba (MG), Ribeirão Preto (SP) e Paulínia (SP), que recebem etanol das usinas produtoras do país.

O biocombustível é transportado por dutos até os polos de distribuição de Barueri, Guarulhos, São Caetano do Sul e São José dos Campos, no Estado de São Paulo, e de Duque de Caxias (RJ), além do terminal marítimo da Ilha D’Água (RJ), onde é carregado em navios-tanque para cabotagem e exportação.

Segundo a Petrobras , a transação trará "relevantes sinergias operacionais" e permitirá a integração da malha dutoviária da Logum ao Sistema Petrobras .

O valor total da aquisição, de R$ 620 milhões , será pago em três parcelas: R$ 300 milhões no fechamento da operação, R$ 160 milhões após 12 meses e R$ 160 milhões após 24 meses.

O negócio ainda depende da aprovação do Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade).

articles.title: Is AI putting Indian IT jobs at risk? What Moody’s says about the future of work
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: AI may be making workplaces smarter, but it has also kept employees on their toes since its advent, leaving many wondering if their jobs are
articles.body: NEW DELHI: AI may be making workplaces smarter, but it has also kept employees on their toes since its advent, leaving many wondering if their jobs are next on the chopping block.This could be a particular concern for countries such as India, where IT services and business-process outsourcing (BPO) are major sectors. However, AI's impact on jobs and productivity is not clearly visible in India yet, Moody’s Ratings said on Thursday.The bigger challenge for emerging economies could be getting the basics right to benefit from AI. Access to computing power, digital infrastructure and skilled workers will increasingly decide how much countries can gain from the technology, Moody’s said in its Global Emerging Markets Outlook 2027 report.The agency expects economic growth in the largest emerging market economies to remain largely unchanged in 2027 compared with 2026. However, growth could be better if the conflict in the Middle East eases. Moody’s has already raised its GDP growth forecast for India in FY27 to 7% from 6.5% earlier.Can AI be a boost or a job threat?For countries that depend heavily on software, IT services and BPO, AI could have two sides. While it may help businesses improve productivity, it could also lead to job losses.India and the Philippines are among the emerging economies that could face the biggest impact because of their exposure to these sectors. But there is no clear evidence of either trend so far, Moody’s said."For EMs with significant levels of software or IT and business-process outsourcing exposures, AI could both raise productivity and create displacement risks. But even for India and the Philippines — the potentially most-exposed EM countries — there is no current clear illustration of either trend," Moody's said.Demand for commodities will continue to support some emerging economies, particularly countries that produce metals and energy. However, growth is expected to remain slow and differ considerably from one country to another.Spending by consumers, especially where government policies support it, will also help some economies. Foreign direct investment (FDI) will be another source of growth for countries that attract significant investment.Keeping government debt under control will remain a challenge for emerging economies as interest costs rise.Moody’s expects most emerging market governments to keep their debt levels stable by controlling spending, taking steps to increase revenue or doing both.However, governments may not have enough room to deal with fresh economic shocks. Rigid spending commitments could limit their ability to respond to events such as a possible record El Nino."The fiscal space for policy responses to further shocks, such as the potential impact of a record El Nino, may however be constrained due to rigid spending structures. Some of the larger EM sovereigns will choose to keep their spending above revenues which, along with higher interest costs, will increase their debt," Moody's said.Brazil, China and India are among the major emerging economies expected to see their public debt increase. This will be due to a combination of spending more than they earn and paying higher interest on existing debt.For China and India, higher interest payments are expected to add more to their debt than budget deficits.AI investment to support global growthIn a separate Global Sovereign Outlook report, Moody’s said the global economy is expected to maintain steady growth in 2027.Healthy finances of banks, companies and households, along with governments' response to the energy shock caused by the Middle East conflict, will support economic activity. Investment in AI and a gradual return of oil supplies to normal levels are also expected to help.These factors could allow governments to keep their debt levels stable in 2027.However, higher interest rates, lower-than-expected returns from AI investments and fresh geopolitical tensions remain key risks to the outlook."Risks include higher interest rates, weaker than expected AI investment returns with economic and financial spillovers and renewed geopolitical shocks," it added.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Chinese ‘spy’ Alice's husband introduced her to Nvidia CEO; flaunted their relationship to clients: Report
articles.summary: Suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang was introduced to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang through her husband, corporate investor Kang Weigh, around a decade before
articles.body: Suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang was introduced to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang through her husband, corporate investor Kang Weigh, around a decade before reports of her alleged relationship with the billionaire executive emerged, according to a report by The New York Post, citing The Information.Kang had business dealings with Jensen in the 2010s while acquiring Chinese video game companies, a source familiar with the couple told The Information.Chinese media reports suggest that Kang and Alice leveraged their association with Jensen to secure business opportunities over the years. Some social media posts claimed that Kang would flaunt his wife's relationship with the Nvidia CEO to their clients, while Alice herself regularly shared photographs with Jensen on her WeChat account.Her proximity to the Nvidia CEO was allegedly a major factor in her business dealings in China.Alice's recent dealings with Jensen reportedly took place through Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company that conducted billions of dollars in business with Nvidia.Megaspeed has faced allegations of smuggling high-end chips to China in violation of US export restrictions, with around 50,000 chips reportedly unaccounted for during an audit. The company has denied wrongdoing and said it complies with all regulations.Before joining Megaspeed, Alice was a senior executive and equity partner at Shanghai Hexi Investment. The firm and its leadership had previously faced regulatory action. In 2018, Kang's company was fined $2.6 million, while he was personally fined $60,000 over disclosure violations and illegal trading linked to the takeover of Huiqiu Technology. In 2025, China's securities regulator fined Hexi another $350,000 for failing to disclose an insider stake in an acquired company.Alice, who previously worked as a reporter for Chinese state broadcaster CCTV and regional channel Hunan TV, reportedly had no experience in the artificial intelligence sector before 2023, when Megaspeed was established.The reports have emerged after Jensen acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife of 40 years. Meanwhile, allegations that Alice was working as a Chinese spy have been denied by the Chinese embassy.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Everyone wanted a Labubu. What happened to the dolls that took the internet by storm?
articles.summary: The Labubu fever finally seems to be cooling off.
articles.body: The Labubu fever finally seems to be cooling off. The furry dolls that once had collectors queuing up, spending big and hunting for rare editions are gradually losing their appeal. With sales falling and newer collectibles gaining popularity, Pop Mart's biggest hit is struggling to maintain its earlier excitement.Collectors, young and old, once rushed to buy 'blind boxes,' sealed mystery packages containing the quirky dolls, often paying $15 (£11) or more. Those who failed to find their favourite characters were willing to spend considerably more in the resale market.The craze these devilish looking dolls had was nothing less than massive!One North Carolina fan told BBC that he even quit his technology job in 2024 to become a full-time Labubu content creator. He travelled to Italy and Spain in search of new releases and spent more than $50,000 (£37,000) building a collection of over 400 dolls. He even got a dentist to make him customised jagged teeth resembling those of Labubus.However, his once-viral videos are no longer attracting the same attention. "Those videos used to be able to hit 10,000 really quickly but I'm struggling to do that now." Ensito has since shifted his focus to other collectibles, including Hello Kitty and squishies.The slowdown reflects a wider challenge for Pop Mart, whose popularity had once pushed its valuation above that of US toy giants Hasbro and Mattel combined. The Beijing-based company recently reported that global sales in the three months to the end of September fell by as much as 50% year-on-year.US revenue dropped by at least 70%.From blind boxes to a global sensationAlthough Pop Mart did not invent blind boxes, its Labubu dolls helped popularise the concept worldwide. The mystery of not knowing which character was inside each package added to the excitement, while the experience reminded collectors of opening gifts as children, says marketing professional Katelynn Carlson, who owns 36 Labubus.Launched in 2019, Labubu became Pop Mart's most successful toy line. The monsters soon turned into fashion accessories, sported by celebrities such as Kim Kardashian and Blackpink's Lisa. Their popularity led to long queues outside stores, and Pop Mart temporarily withdrew the dolls from its UK shops following reports of customers fighting over them. One collector even paid more than $150,000 for a human-sized Labubu.According to Samer El Hajjar, a marketing lecturer at the National University of Singapore, cited by BBC the difficulty of finding certain editions was a major part of their appeal. Collectors repeatedly bought blind boxes in the hope of finding their preferred characters.Pop Mart now has more than 670 shops and at least 2,800 vending machines worldwide. Listed in Hong Kong in 2020, the company is valued at nearly $24 billion. However, its shares have fallen by more than 50% from last year's peak.Investors are concerned that its global success may have been driven by a viral moment rather than lasting customer loyalty, El Hajjar says.The loss of exclusivity has also affected the excitement, according to Ensito. "Now it doesn't feel that way. I walk into a Pop Mart and there's a whole series of Labubus sitting there," he says.Ashley Dudarenok of China research firm ChoZan says Pop Mart's decision to increase production to meet demand weakened the dolls' sense of exclusivity.New collectibles take centre stageAs the Labubu craze fades, other toys are attracting buyers. Sonny Angels, tiny unclothed cherub-like dolls, and miniature glow-in-the-dark Smiski figurines are gaining popularity. My Little Pony and KPop Demon Hunters characters have also entered the blind-box market.Miniso, which was founded in Guangzhou, China, sells Disney and Marvel blind-box collectibles across more than 8,000 stores globally."Consumers aren't particularly concerned about where the brand comes from," Miniso executive Vincent Huang said earlier this year. "They're more focused on the shopping experience - the designs, value for money, and enjoyment."Experts say Pop Mart's biggest challenge is creating characters that can maintain their popularity over time. Analyst Boustani points to Sanrio, the company behind Hello Kitty, which reported record earnings in the year to March, as having an advantage in this area.Pop Mart has been trying to expand its brand through investments such as a theme park in Beijing and an announced Labubu film. However, Dudarenok says the company is taking a different approach from Disney, which builds stories around characters before selling toys."The real test for next year is whether Pop Mart can make people love a character without a celebrity holding it," BBC reported.Collectors become more selectiveThe fading excitement has also prompted collectors to rethink their spending habits.Ensito says he is questioning how much time and money people invest in collections whenever a new trend emerges. "There's always going to be a trend every year. There's always gonna be something that's gonna be really popular."Melbourne-based content creator Lawrence Yu, who owns around 50 dolls, says he plans to be "more selective" after spending two years chasing Labubus. His shopping and unboxing videos once attracted up to a million views, but he rarely creates such content now."I definitely think the trend has slowed down... People go crazy and then it fizzles."Canadian collector Clara Barbero considers Labubus a "dead trend" but continues to look for interesting releases. "I’m curating my collection more and only buying what I see myself liking for the next few years, and not just buying the newest series that’s out."However, the slowdown has not dampened everyone's enthusiasm. Hedy Khaled from Liverpool remains attached to her collection of 70 Pop Mart figurines and believes there is a difference between trend-followers and "real fans".Carlson also continues to enjoy collecting the dolls, particularly new releases such as the cat-themed Labubu series, which has become one of her favourites."I think there's something special about embracing our inner child and enjoying things simply because they make us happy."Money habits form by age 7. articles.summary: Frammer AI, a video automation startup founded by former NDTV executives, has introduced a platform for live sports coverage and signed Malaysian
articles.body: Frammer AI, a video automation startup founded by former NDTV executives, has introduced a platform for live sports coverage and signed Malaysian broadcaster Astro as its first customer, the companies said on Thursday.The platform processes live broadcast feeds to generate match highlights, vertical videos, clips featuring individual players or specific match events, and branded content for social media.Frammer said its technology can turn a moment from a live event into social media content in less than 30 seconds, allowing highlights to be shared while a match is still underway.For Astro, the platform offers a way to generate additional content from sports broadcasting rights for which it has made substantial investments.The broadcaster reaches 5.1 million homes, covering about 61% of Malaysia's television households. It holds the rights to broadcast the Premier League in Malaysia through the 2027/28 season and AFC competitions through 2028/29."Our collaboration with Frammer enables us to deliver timely match highlights and key moments," said Nivendran Veerappan, vice president and head of broadcast and platform engineering at Astro.Frammer CEO and co-founder Suparna Singh said the company wanted to deliver "much more content and audience value for our clients from every hour of sport they have invested so heavily in." She said that, in sports, value depends on the live moment and how quickly audiences can access and share it.The sports platform follows a plan Frammer announced in October 2024, when it raised $2 million in a seed funding round led by Lumikai, a venture fund focused on gaming and interactive media. At the time, the company said it would use the funds to expand into sports and entertainment.Established in 2023, Frammer was founded by Singh, NDTV's former CEO and president; Kawaljit Singh Bedi, the broadcaster's former technology chief; and Arijit Chatterjee, its former chief strategy officer.The company's business has primarily focused on helping news and entertainment publishers convert long-form videos into short, vertical clips for social media platforms. Its offerings also cover streaming, automatically generated free ad-supported streaming television (FAST) channels and distribution across multiple platforms.Frammer estimates that the sports streaming market will be worth about $40 billion this year, supported by the emergence of new leagues and formats and rising interest in niche sports.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Google, Microsoft & more: Valuation of firms led by Indian-origin CEOs hits $15 trillion
articles.summary: From the AI race to the boardroom, Indian-origin business leaders are making their mark on the global corporate map.
articles.body: From the AI race to the boardroom, Indian-origin business leaders are making their mark on the global corporate map. The top companies they head are now worth a combined $15 trillion, a 53% jump in just two years, with the artificial intelligence boom emerging as a major driver of the rise, according to the HSBC Hurun Global Indians List 2026 released on Thursday.Alphabet, headed by Sundar Pichai, leads the list with a valuation of $4.2 trillion. Microsoft, led by Satya Nadella, follows with $2.6 trillion, while Sanjay Mehrotra-led Micron Technology ranks third at $1.4 trillion.The combined valuation of the companies stood at $9.9 trillion two years ago. The latest edition of the list uses June 25 as its cut-off date.AI drives 71% of the total valuationAI is also becoming a major part of the business landscape represented in the rankings. More than half of the 200 companies featured, 103 in total, are either driven by AI or have integrated the technology into their operations. Their combined valuation stands at $10.7 trillion, accounting for 71% of the total value of the companies on the list.Beyond their valuations, these businesses have a substantial economic footprint. Together, they generate $2.5 trillion in annual revenue and employ 53 lakh people."The reach of the global Indians is something most people experience without realising it," Hurun India's Founder and Chief Researcher Anas Rahman Junaid said.76 companies make their debutThe latest list also reflects the entry of several new businesses. As many as 76 companies feature for the first time in this edition. Of the 200 companies, 127 are publicly listed, while 73 are privately held. The list includes 49 startups, whose combined valuation stands at $398 billion.Getting into the list has also become more difficult. The minimum valuation required for entry has risen to $2.5 billion, more than double the $1.2 billion threshold in the previous edition released two years ago.The list covers 236 individuals leading these 200 companies, with professionals accounting for the largest share at 53%. This includes business leaders such as Pichai and Nadella. First-generation entrepreneurs make up 44% of the entrants, while second-generation leaders account for the remaining 3%.US leads, San Francisco tops city rankingsGeographically, the US dominates the rankings with 177 entrants. California alone is home to more than a third of the individuals featured in the list. San Francisco has the highest concentration of diaspora business leaders, with 40 entrants, followed by Dubai with 15. Palo Alto and London have 13 each.The list also highlights the educational institutions represented among these business leaders. articles.title: Worried AI will take your job? Tony Robbins says it's time for a reinvention plan.
articles.summary: Entrepreneur and best-selling author Tony Robbins weighs in on the outlook for job seekers.
articles.body:
Listen and subscribe to Power Players with Brian Sozzi on Apple Podcasts , Amazon Music , Spotify , YouTube , or wherever you find your favorite podcasts.

Entrepreneur and bestselling author Tony Robbins has a message for those worried that AI will take their jobs: Take a hard look at your job, and then design a reinvention plan.

"I think no one is going to be replaced by AI. They're going to be replaced by somebody using AI," Robbins said on the Power Players With Brian Sozzi podcast (see video above or listen below). "Everybody said go become a software engineer, figure out how to write code, and you're going to have a guaranteed job. And then all of a sudden our agents do it for us overnight. But the best code writers now are running 50 agents, and they're doing more in a day than they could have done in the five years before. And so those people are invaluable. I think what you have to do is you have to be looking at what it is you do. And you've got to be honest."

2026 has been dominated by large-scale layoffs at Microsoft ( MSFT ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Meta ( META ), and many other major companies tapping into AI to do more work with fewer people. Experts believe the pruning of workforces at the hands of AI will persist in the year ahead.

In fact, Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) CEO Dario Amodei has famously predicted that AI could wipe out half of white-collar jobs and push unemployment to 20%.

Robbins has a first-hand look into the emotions of the employed and unemployed. He is a motivational speaker, bestselling author, and entrepreneur.

CEOs and elite leaders — from financial titans like Paul Tudor Jones to tech founders like Salesforce ( CRM ) co-founder Marc Benioff — have turned to him. Robbins bypasses traditional management theory to focus on cognitive restructuring and psychological conditioning. An approach proponents say helps high performers break through mental blocks to make high-stakes decisions under pressure.

Robbins thinks now is the time for workers to retool their skill sets to withstand the AI shift and thrive in it.

"If I drive a taxi or Uber or something of that nature, I got to be able to be honest with myself and say, that job is not going to exist in five years more than likely because of self-driving trucks, for example," Robbins said. "And that's just one industry that's obviously going to be disrupted."

articles.title: Qualcomm CEO: Elon Musk is serious about SpaceX's cellular network ambitions
articles.summary: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon sees Starlink being a big deal.
articles.body:
Qualcomm ( QCOM ) CEO Cristiano Amon thinks Elon Musk is super serious about being a major player in the cellular business with SpaceX's ( SPCX ) Starlink.

"If you look at Starlink and what they have done in communication, that's a very, very important telecom business. It's kind of a natural evolution of that," Amon said at Yahoo Finance Invest.

Earlier this month, Qualcomm signed a multiyear agreement with SpaceX to supply radio equipment, baseband units, and software for Starlink's planned nationwide 5G network.

Musk called Qualcomm's technology "excellent" in a response to Amon on X. The equipment will begin being deployed in 2027.

"I think what's happening is SpaceX is building a nationwide terrestrial network. It's a 5G nationwide terrestrial network in the United States. It's among the largest deployments of infrastructure in the United States," Amon said, adding, "It's a great partnership, and I think it's going to continue to drive innovation cycle in the cellular industry."

Musk has spent the last few months sending clear messages to legacy telecom players like T-Mobile ( TMUS ), AT&T ( T ) and Verizon ( VZ ).

The company is looking to lease space on 80,000 cell sites across the US. Bloomberg reported in late October that SpaceX is reportedly in talks with two of the largest owners of cellular towers, Crown Castle ( CCI ) and American Tower ( AMT ).

Why CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz is looking forward to Anthropic and OpenAI going public

'The world is not going to end in 2030': CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz on Anthropic IPO's warning to humanity

'If the race is there, you win it': CrowdStrike CEO and Mercedes F1 investor George Kurtz on driving phenom Kimi Antonelli

"Committing ~$30 billion into spectrum is serious enough. Committing to 80K macro sites could be a point of no return," Bernstein analyst Laurent Yoon wrote. "That is a meaningful number, broadly consistent with the scale required for a nationwide terrestrial wireless network. Whether SpaceX ultimately leases anything close to that figure remains uncertain, but the reported scope suggests a far greater level of commitment than spectrum accumulation alone."

SpaceX also recently acquired a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio.

"Starlink broadband is the threat investors can see today and one that incumbents are beginning to acknowledge," Yoon said. "Starlink Mobile remains the larger long-term question given the size and profitability of the wireless market. The competitive impact may still be years away, but anticipation alone, reinforced by each successive spectrum and infrastructure move, is likely to remain an overhang on sector sentiment."

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Huang resigns amid affair scandals, board names CFO Colette Kress interim CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is resigning following reports that he had an affair with a fellow executive at the AI giant and after he admitted to having a separa...
articles.body:
Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO following reports that he had an affair with a fellow executive at the AI giant and after he admitted to having a separate affair with a woman whom US intelligence officials believe is a Chinese spy.

CFO Colette Kress will succeed Huang as interim CEO until the company names a permanent CEO. The chip giant is looking both internally and externally for candidates.

Nvidia also named Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever board chair. Jones previously served as CEO and executive chair of Synopsys.

Nvidia stock plunged more than 12% in early trading.

"Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position," Jones said in a statement.

"She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption."

Kress, in a statement, said she is committed to building on the work Huang has done to turn Nvidia into the company it has become.

"We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders," she said.

According to the New York Times , Huang engaged in a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who heads the company's healthcare efforts.

On Sunday, Huang issued a statement admitting to the initial affair, apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees.

According to reports, the woman Huang was seeing, Alice Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based technology firm MegaSpeed and was allegedly acting as a spy on behalf of the Chinese government.

Nvidia's board has said it has launched an independent investigation into the matter, but added it has no reason to believe Nvidia trade secrets or national security were compromised.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, with a vision to bring 3D graphics to the gaming industry.

The company primarily focused on the space for years before releasing its CUDA technology in 2006, allowing users to take advantage of Nvidia's graphics chips for general-purpose computing.

The company took that a step further in 2013 with the release of its first AI server, the DGX-1. Both CUDA and the DGX-1 gave Nvidia an early lead in the AI hardware race when OpenAI launched its ChatGPT in late 2022.

articles.body: Nvidia share price crash: Shares of Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, crashed in opening trade on Thursday as its CEO Jensen Huang resigned. At the stock market opening, shares of Nvidia were trading at $150.98, down 13.09%.This marks a major leadership change for the AI industry and raises questions about the future of the chipmaker Huang transformed into a dominant force in artificial intelligence. The stock crash has taken the market value of Nvidia to below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.The company said on Thursday that Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress would serve as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement.Nvidia also appointed former Synopysys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as the company's first chairman of the board.Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and holds a stake of around 3.61%, making him its fourth-largest investor, will also step down from the board.Nvidia shares plunged more than 12.89% in premarket trading, adding to pressure on the wider stock market.Jensen Huang scandalScrutiny of Huang had intensified in recent days following reports alleging that the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing.A person familiar with the matter told Reuters that Nvidia's board convened on Wednesday to discuss removing Huang. This followed reports earlier that day alleging that he had also been involved in an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported directly to him.Huang's departure leaves the $4 trillion company facing uncertainty and threatens to unsettle the wider AI ecosystem that he helped finance. Nvidia has channelled its growing cash reserves back into the industry, investing in cloud service providers, suppliers and some of the world's largest AI research labs.Investor confidence in AI-related stocks has already weakened amid concerns about mounting cash burn and increasing debt among technology companies that have traditionally generated substantial cash. These developments have raised questions about whether the massive investments underpinning the AI boom will ultimately deliver the expected returns.Huang's exit could also have significant implications for US policy on chip exports, given his efforts to maintain access to the Chinese market and his close relationship with US President Donald Trump.On Sunday, Trump said Huang had "done an amazing job for our country". He also said the Nvidia chief had told him he was unaware that the Chinese woman with whom he had an affair was a spy.A departure by Huang could "leave a vacuum at the top", said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth a few hours before the announcement of Huang’s resignation."They're going to have to find a successor that will help the market feel comfortable in the leadership and the direction the company will take."Beyond the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia, investors are increasingly concerned that the broader AI industry could lose momentum. articles.title: Planning Nvidia investigations, top Democrats tell Trump administration to 'preserve all records'
articles.summary: Democrats have formally asked the Trump administration to "preserve all records" related to its dealings with Nvidia as Democrats prepare to take power on Ca...
articles.body:
Democratic Sens. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Chris Coons of Delaware have formally asked the Trump administration to "preserve all records" related to the administration's dealings with Nvidia ( NVDA ) as Democrats prepare to take power on Capitol Hill in 2027 and promise to probe the issues surrounding CEO Jensen Huang's departure.

The request came in a letter Wednesday evening targeting any administration materials related to the chipmaker's exports to China, as well as the ousted CEO's affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.

Huang's resignation "does not absolve him, other executives, or the company as a whole of responsibility for putting our national security at risk or for any potential violations of our laws," Warren said in a statement Thursday morning adding that Trump officials must still "explain why they have not closed export control loopholes."

The letter was directed to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller and noted reports that Trump officials were aware of concerns about Nvidia, "yet did not move to block the continued flow of advanced AI chips to Megaspeed or other companies affiliated with the suspected operative."

The White House didn't offer an immediate response Thursday morning. The letter asked the officials to confirm by next Tuesday that they will comply and have begun the document preservation process.

Huang stepped down as CEO on Thursday as the scandal over his extramarital affairs quickly besieged one of the world's most valuable companies and its founder.

Warren and Coons are in line to be the heads of the Senate's powerful Banking and Foreign Relations committees and will oversee any investigations with subpoena power.

Meanwhile, the still-unfolding scandal has multiple prongs that touch the White House and the Trump administration.

Huang lobbied President Trump to loosen limits on advanced chips, and the White House allowed Nvidia to ship certain versions to China and other countries deemed security risks.

Trump reportedly didn't take action when he learned about the possibility of a security breach and has repeatedly defended Huang in recent days, calling him "an honorable guy."

Axios reported that Trump last week ordered a crackdown on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China, but that it was Lutnick who stood in the way and at least slow-walked the order's execution.

That turned the focus on Lutnick, who will be under perhaps the most direct scrutiny in the months ahead.

articles.title: Karnataka’s per capita alcohol consumption falls 2.4%
articles.summary: Karnataka per capita pure alcohol consumption fell 2.4% to 1.59L in May–Sept 2026 after AIB tax; excise revenue rose 13.4% to Rs 22,191.63 crore.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Karnataka’s per capita consumption of pure alcohol declined 2.4% in the five months to Sept after the introduction of a new tax system that links duties to alcohol content, according to data analysed by the Brewers Association of India (BAI).Consumption of pure alcohol per person fell to 1.59 litres between May and Sept 2026, compared with 1.63 litres in the corresponding period last year, the industry body said.The decline came even as the state’s excise revenue rose 13.4% year-on-year to Rs 22,191.63 crore during April-Sept, suggesting that the new taxation system could be helping the govt increase collections while encouraging a shift towards drinks with lower alcohol content.Karnataka introduced the new Alcohol-in-Beverage (AIB) taxation system on May 11, under which taxes are linked to the quantity of alcohol contained in a beverage.The change has prompted consumers and manufacturers to shift towards lower-strength drinks, BAI said.Beer and wine now account for 45% of total alcoholic beverage sales, up from 36% a year earlier. At the same time, several manufacturers of economy Indian-made foreign liquor (IMFL) have reduced the alcohol strength of their products from 42.8% to 40%.Consequently, the average alcoholic strength of IMFL sold in Karnataka has fallen to 40.5%, according to the association.“It is a remarkable fall for such a short period. There are several global precedents for a rapid reduction in alcohol consumption after taxes are linked with alcohol content. Still, the speed at which it has fallen in Karnataka is impressive,” said Vinod Giri, director general of BAI.The association said that while the volume of alcoholic beverages sold increased 16%, the quantity of pure alcohol contained in those beverages declined 2.4%. This reflects a shift towards weaker alcoholic drinks rather than necessarily a reduction in the volume of beverages purchased.IMFL case sales grew 1.1% during April-Sept, compared with a 1% decline in the corresponding period last year. BAI said the findings suggest that linking taxes to alcohol strength could help state govts increase revenue while encouraging manufacturers to lower the alcohol content of their products.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Turkey secures record $1.6 billion AIIB financing for climate reforms at COP31
articles.summary: Turkey has announced a groundbreaking $1.6 billion financing deal with the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) to bolster its climate initiatives and attract private investments amidst rising climate challenges.
articles.body: Turkey has secured a $1.6 billion financing agreement from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) to support policy reforms and attract private investment for its climate targets.The funding will help Turkey address an estimated $68 billion investment requirement for climate action by 2030, with around half of the amount expected to come from private sources, according to the AIIB. The agreement was announced on Thursday, the fourth day of the two-week UN climate conference in Antalya.The programme covers fiscal policy, financial regulation and sectoral planning. It is intended to support the implementation of Turkey's Climate Law and its emissions reduction strategy, which includes an interim target for 2035 and a commitment to reach net-zero emissions by 2053.The financing will be directed towards expanding sustainable finance, reducing emissions across industries and strengthening the country's ability to deal with climate-related risks. Turkey, which has a population of around 86 million, faces growing exposure to droughts, floods and wildfires as global temperatures rise.Konstantin Limitovskiy, AIIB's chief investment officer, said the agreement was the bank's largest climate policy-based financing package to date.The deal comes as the bank expands its climate-related lending. Its total climate financing reached a record $7.47 billion in 2025, according to the statement.Support for Turkey's emissions trading systemA portion of the funding will help Turkey develop its emissions trading system, which is still in its early stages. Under the proposed mechanism, companies operating in high-emission industries will receive allowances that can be traded.The system could also have implications for Turkish exporters supplying goods such as steel and cement to the European Union. Under the EU's carbon border levy, carbon costs paid in Turkey can be recognised when calculating charges on emissions embedded in certain imported products. A domestic carbon pricing mechanism could therefore help exporters account for these costs.The programme has set several targets for the coming years. At least 180 industrial facilities are expected to report their baseline emissions under the trading scheme by April 2027. The plan also aims to secure production licences for 1,800 megawatts of wind and solar power capacity by early 2027.Agriculture and land management are also included in the reforms. The programme aims to help 225,000 farmers in water-stressed areas shift to crops that require less water by 2028. It also targets the designation of 50,000 hectares of land as carbon sinks by the same year, allowing these areas to absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.Climate risks drive policy reformsTurkey is facing mounting pressure from water shortages, prolonged drought, extreme heat, wildfires and flooding in urban areas. The reform programme is designed to strengthen planning and risk management across sectors affected by these threats, including water resources, ecosystems and public health.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Chinese 'spy' Alice Huang's companies invested in DeepSeek, promised Nvidia's Blackwell chips
articles.summary: Companies linked to alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang have invested in Chinese artificial intelligence firm DeepSeek and committed to supplying Nvidia's
articles.body: Companies linked to alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang have invested in Chinese artificial intelligence firm DeepSeek and committed to supplying Nvidia's Blackwell chips, according to a report by The Information.Blackwell is Nvidia's latest generation of graphics processing units (GPUs) and AI accelerators. Built on the company's Blackwell GPU microarchitecture, it succeeds the older Hopper architecture and is designed to power large-scale artificial intelligence, heavy-duty data centres and high-performance computing.Alice, also known as Alice Wang or Huang Le, is a Chinese businesswoman whose links with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed have come under scrutiny.Meanwhile, Singapore authorities have issued Alice a stern warning and barred her from re-entering the country after finding that she provided inaccurate information during investigations into Megaspeed.Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said the Singapore Police Force (SPF) assessed that Alice had attempted to mislead investigators to downplay her role in the company.The probe centres on suspected false declarations involving the purchase of servers and other related offences. The SPF and Singapore Customs launched separate investigations into Megaspeed and others in February 2025.Alice's association with the Nvidia CEO reportedly dates back several years. According to reports, she was introduced to Jensen through her husband, corporate investor Kang Weigh, around a decade before reports of her alleged relationship with the billionaire executive emerged.Kang had business dealings with Jensen in the 2010s while acquiring Chinese video game companies, a source familiar with the couple told The Information.Chinese media reports suggest that Kang and Alice used their association with Jensen to secure business opportunities over the years. Some social media posts claimed that Kang would flaunt his wife's relationship with the Nvidia CEO to clients. Alice also regularly shared photographs with Jensen on her WeChat account.Her proximity to Jensen was allegedly a major factor in her business dealings in China.Their more recent business dealings reportedly took place through Megaspeed, which conducted billions of dollars in business with Nvidia. The Singapore-based data centre company remains under investigation over suspected false declarations linked to server purchases.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: 'Legend replaces a legend': Trump wants Tim Cook to replace Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has brought Apple's Tim Cook into the conversation around Nvidia's leadership, suggesting that the Apple CEO should replace
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has brought Apple's Tim Cook into the conversation around Nvidia's leadership, suggesting that the Apple CEO should replace Jensen Huang at the chipmaker.In a post on Truth Social, Trump called Cook the only person fit to take over from Huang, who has resigned with immediate effect.“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! President DONALD J. TRUMP “Trump's suggestion comes after Cook stepped down as Apple’s chief back in September after leading the Cupertino-based company for more than a decade. Trump also recalled his association with Cook, describing him as “an incredible guy” and saying their professional relationship began during his first term as president, when Cook approached him for help with an issue.Nvidia's sudden leadership changeNvidia's board announced on Thursday that Jensen Huang had stepped down as the chipmaker's president, CEO and board member, with the resignation taking immediate effect.The announcement followed reports of two alleged affairs involving Huang. One involves a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing. Another report alleged that Huang had an extramarital relationship with a senior company executive who reported directly to him.A person familiar with the matter said Nvidia's board had met on Wednesday to consider Huang's removal.The company acknowledged the contributions of its outgoing chief, saying, “Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. Shares of Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, crashed in opening trade on Thursday as its CEO Jensen Huang resigned.“NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” it added.The board has named chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and owns around 3.61% of the company, is its fourth-largest investor. He will also give up his board position.Huang's departure was followed by a steep fall in Nvidia shares during Thursday's opening trade. The stock dropped 13.09% to $150.98, taking the company's market capitalisation below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.The exit marks a major leadership change for the AI industry, particularly for Nvidia, which Huang transformed into a dominant force in artificial intelligence.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Norwest to hike investments in Indian manufacturing, healthcare and tech after $4bn global fund raise
articles.summary: MUMBAI: US-based Norwest has raised a record $4 billion fund, its largest in 65 years, part of which will be used to expand investments in India,
articles.body: MUMBAI: US-based Norwest has raised a record $4 billion fund, its largest in 65 years, part of which will be used to expand investments in India, particularly in manufacturing, industrial services and healthcare. It currently deploys $250-350 million annually in the country.Norwest 18 takes the firm's capital under management to $18 billion and will fund venture and growth equity investments across technology, healthcare and consumer sectors in the US, India and Israel.The firm has maintained steady investments across market cycles for two decades, said Niren Shah, managing director and head of Norwest India. "Norwest is currently deploying around $250-350 million annually in India, which is higher than the earlier levels of investment. Norwest remains very bullish on India's long-term prospects," he said.While fintech and consumer remain core sectors, Norwest is increasing its focus on industrials and healthcare. It will pursue growth equity, venture, platform and buyout investments. "Industrials and Healthcare are becoming increasingly prominent in our investment strategy. Norwest will continue to remain a Multi-strategy fund and focus both on Growth Equity and Venture investments, while also looking to undertake more Platform and Buyout transactions," Shah said.The firm sees opportunities in value-added and precision manufacturing and industrial services, driven by Make in India and global manufacturers' growing emphasis on quality and supply-chain diversification over cost alone. "Our investment approach will continue to be centred on Growth Equity, with a greater focus on Precision Manufacturing and Industrial services," Shah said. Healthcare and fintech will remain priorities, alongside venture investments in AI and deep tech.Since launching Norwest 17 in April 2024, the firm has made over 87 investments and helped more than 30 portfolio companies achieve exits through IPOs and acquisitions. These include Indian listings Swiggy and Amagi Media Labs, US listings BillionToOne, MBX Biosciences and Omada Health, and acquisitions of Qualified by Salesforce, Veza by ServiceNow and Ouro Medicines by Gilead Sciences.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Decline in oil prices could save India up to $9bn in FY27
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Moderation in international crude oil prices could save India up to $9 billion on its oil import bill in the current fiscal and help temper
articles.body: MUMBAI: Moderation in international crude oil prices could save India up to $9 billion on its oil import bill in the current fiscal and help temper wholesale price inflation, even as the impact on retail inflation is likely to remain limited, according to a Bank of Baroda research report.The report, authored by economist Dipanwita Mazumdar, estimates that a 10% decline in international oil prices from current levels could reduce India's oil import bill by $9-10 billion, equivalent to around 0.2% of nominal GDP. This would also support the current account deficit (CAD).International oil prices fell 22.2% between Oct 30 and Nov 10, following expectations of a possible peace agreement between the US and Iran after the US midterm elections. However, escalating attacks involving Saudi-led forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen could affect the sustainability of the decline. Brent crude futures were trading around $81 per barrel.The moderation in oil prices is expected to have a greater impact on wholesale price inflation (WPI) than consumer price inflation (CPI). Oil-sensitive components account for around 8.8% of the WPI basket. A 10% decline in crude prices could lower WPI inflation by 13-14 basis points through direct and indirect effects on petroleum products, aviation turbine fuel (ATF) and manufactured goods.The impact on CPI is expected to be largely neutral because retail prices of petrol, diesel and LPG are administered. Restaurant prices are also unlikely to respond to a temporary decline in oil prices, while the pass-through to airfares will depend on airlines and demand conditions.The report noted that consumers were largely insulated when international crude prices rose sharply, as retail fuel prices remained unchanged. A decline in global prices is therefore unlikely to translate into lower retail selling prices. However, the correction could narrow the divergence between CPI and WPI, offering some relief to manufacturers whose input costs had risen without a corresponding increase in consumer prices.On the fiscal front, higher fertiliser subsidies could increase the fiscal deficit by 0.2-0.3% of GDP. The FY27 Budget had allocated Rs 1.7 lakh crore for urea and fertiliser subsidies, including Rs 1.2 lakh crore for urea and Rs 54,000 crore under the nutrient-based subsidy (NBS) scheme.The NBS allocation has since increased to Rs 1.03 lakh crore, including Rs 41,534 crore for the kharif season and Rs 62,370 crore for the rabi season. Lower profitability of oil marketing companies could also weigh on non-tax revenue. However, higher nominal GDP growth and disinvestment receipts could provide some support to the fiscal position.Lower oil prices could also support the rupee, alongside a revival in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) inflows. Net FPI inflows rose to $7.1 billion in Nov, compared with outflows of $2.5 billion in Oct. The report attributed the revival partly to greater investor interest in emerging markets amid policy uncertainty in the US and moderation in AI-led valuations.Bank of Baroda expects the rupee to trade in the range of Rs 93-95 against the dollar in the near term, compared with its earlier forecast of Rs 94-95. However, the dollar index and expectations of tighter monetary policy in major economies remain key factors to watch.The impact of lower oil prices on bond yields is expected to be limited. While cheaper crude could provide temporary relief to India's 10-year government bond yield, global yields and domestic monetary policy are likely to keep borrowing costs elevated. The report expects another 50 basis points of rate hikes in FY27, which could limit the decline in yields.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Will Social Security go broke in 2032? What retirees need to know.
articles.summary: The looming shortfall in Social Security benefits is projected to result in a 22% to 26% cut by 2032. What to know about whether Social Security benefits wil...
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

The looming shortfall in Social Security benefits is projected to result in a 22% to 26% cut by 2032, according to the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) and the latest 2026 Social Security Trustees' report.

While fewer workers funding more recipients is widely blamed for the financial pressures facing Social Security, a new study says "shifting income patterns" have also weakened the program's solvency — and offers a solution.

Rising wages among high-income earners often exceed Social Security's taxable cap, Richard W. Johnson of the AARP Public Policy Institute noted in a new analysis. Meanwhile, corporate earnings and investment returns are flourishing.

By lifting the payroll tax cap and taxing some of the investment income of high earners, Social Security could pay full benefits until 2059, 25 years longer than current projections.

"These changes would help close Social Security's financing gap without requiring lower- or moderate-income people to contribute more," Johnson wrote.

Here is what's happening and what needs to be done to save the system every American worker has helped fund.

In short: Fewer workers are funding more recipients.

In 1960, there were 5.1 workers paying into the system for every Social Security recipient. That ratio fell throughout the 1980s and 1990s, and when the oldest baby boomers turned 62 in 2008, a dramatic decline began.

In 2024, there were 2.7 workers per beneficiary.

With longer lifetimes and fewer workers per Social Security recipient, the financial drain on the system is dramatic.

As the AARP report observed, national income distribution over the past 40 years has also contributed to Social Security's dwindling revenue.

"Although payroll taxes paid primarily by middle-income workers currently account for 91% of Social Security revenue, the relative economic position of these workers has steadily declined."

A recent UCLA/Cornell study confirmed the widely held belief that most people think Social Security is going broke and expect "benefits to cease completely" when it does.

What most people don't consider, the research concluded, are the funds continuing to flow into the system.

Even if reserve funds are depleted, American workers will continue to pay into Social Security through payroll taxes deducted from their paychecks each payday. That means Social Security benefits will continue to be paid, but are likely to be reduced.

"Benefits will continue to be payable after reserve depletion, but not in full unless legislative action is taken," the American Academy of Actuaries noted in an analysis of the SSA's trustees report.

As Social Security collects payroll taxes, it pays out benefits to retired workers and eligible family members, as well as death and disability benefits. Workers pay 6.2% from their wages, and employers match that amount. Self-employed individuals pay the full 12.4% of Social Security taxes. Both are capped at a maximum wage.

Medicare taxes and benefits are also collected.

If Social Security collects more than is paid out in benefits, the excess is placed in trust fund reserves and invested in Treasurys to pay future benefits.

"When people talk of Social Security 'going bankrupt,' they are (incorrectly or misleadingly) referring to a scenario where the Social Security Trust Fund has no reserves (it has become 'depleted') and tax revenue is insufficient to cover existing benefits obligations," the Roosevelt Institute, a nonprofit think tank, explained in an analysis.

The fact is, Social Security can pay full benefits for a few more years but then faces a "significant, though manageable, funding shortfall," the institute added.

If action isn't taken, yes, benefits could be cut.

"If reforms are not enacted soon, recipients could see a large decrease in their benefits," the Peter G. Peterson Foundation, a nonprofit think tank, said in an analysis. "If lawmakers act soon to address the trust fund shortfalls, they will be able to phase in changes gradually and responsibly in a way that does not harm vulnerable populations. However, delaying reform would require larger changes to the program."

"Restoring balance to the Social Security system could involve raising taxes, changing benefits, or a combination of these two approaches," the American Academy of Actuaries reported.

The Academy lists possible ways of increasing revenue into the system:

Increasing taxes paid by high-wage earners

Gradually raising the full retirement age

Lowering the inflation index used to adjust benefits

Under current assumptions, the actuarial organization estimates that it would take an immediate 3.65% increase in the combined employee/employer tax rate (to a total 16.05% of taxable payroll), or an immediate 22.4% cut in benefits to current and future recipients.

Either would "balance the system over the next 75 years," the organization concluded.

The American Academy of Actuaries has a web app that demystifies Social Security through animation and voiceovers. The Social Security Challenge explains how the system works, the looming funding shortfall, and possible financial solutions.

As explained by David Mendes, director of communications for the Academy, the web resource "immerses users in an animated virtual trek where they learn about the program, the financing shortfall that could (if unaddressed by Congress) lead to future cuts in scheduled benefits, and how different reform options they select along their journey could help address the shortfall."

Graphically illustrating the problem and possible solutions may be the only way to truly understand the challenges Social Security faces.

articles.title: Happiest Health gets Rs 500 cr tech boost from Soota
articles.summary: Ashok Soota to invest Rs 500 crore in Happiest Health tech over 5 years, boosting digital health apps like DiaBeater and ColonE after Happiest Minds stake sale.
articles.body: Bengaluru: At 83, Ashok Soota remains upbeat about his healthcare venture, backing it with fresh funds to accelerate growth. He has earmarked Rs 500 crore from the proceeds of the sale of his stake in Happiest Minds to ITC Infotech to accelerate technology investments at Happiest Health over the next five years. About half of this amount will go towards its digital health business, Happiest Digital Health, the company’s fifth business unit, which will begin with a portfolio of 11 digital applications to be rolled out over the next 18 months.Soota said a substantial part of the Rs 1,330 crore proceeds from the sale of his 22.1% stake in Happiest Minds to ITC Infotech would be channelled into healthcare initiatives, including Happiest Health and a non-profit entity, SKAN Research Trust. He had previously committed Rs 200 crore towards SKAN, focused on ageing and neurological research.“Investment will come from the proceeds of the ITC Infotech transaction. Even after the merger, I will remain the single largest individual shareholder in the merged entity. My technology connection will continue. It’s a very important part of the business.”Digital health is a fast-growing segment of healthcare, expected to reach $1.8 trillion globally by 2033, growing at 25% annually, he said. The move is also aimed at overcoming the geographical limitations of physical healthcare providers.“Even companies that have been around for 30 years are present in only two, three or four cities. Some of the largest players derive 44% of their business from one city and another 40% from a second city, with only a small presence elsewhere. So nobody can reach out too far,” Soota said.He said the digital health business would draw on the medical expertise developed within Happiest Health, with doctors guiding the design and clinical content of individual applications. Happiest Minds is developing the technology, including small language models (SLMs), while medical inputs will come from specialists.The company is placing particular emphasis on diabetes management through DiaBeater, a doctor-led, AI-assisted application that uses glucose-monitoring technology. India has more than 100 million people living with diabetes, making continuous care a significant opportunity, Soota said. Dr Kashinath, who heads the endocrinology practice at Happiest Health and has 28 years of experience, including at the UK’s NHS, is guiding the medical framework for the application.Other planned offerings include Pediatric Expert and Cardio Edge. The company is also launching ColonE, a gut microbiome test that uses next-generation sequencing to analyse microbial DNA from a stool sample. The process generates about 5GB of data, which is used to prepare a report that nutritionists draw on to guide dietary and lifestyle changes. ColonE is a wellness offering, not a diagnostic test.SKAN Research Trust has conducted more than 1,000 gut microbiome tests and built a substantial data repository, Soota said. He identified gut microbiome research and bioinformatics as two important areas of work at SKAN, adding that it would remain a non-commercial entity, although monetisation avenues could be explored later.Happiest Health has identified 15-20 additional specialities for potential digital applications, though not all may lend themselves to digital delivery. The company will assess the market size and consumers’ willingness to pay in each segment before firming up revenue projections.Soota said the company expects to prepare internal financial plans by March and may share tentative business projections by June. It also plans to present its broader healthcare services business once six or seven facilities are ready, potentially by mid-2027.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones?
